label: John 19:1
text: So Pilate then took Jesus, and flogged him.

label: John 19:2
text: The soldiers twisted thorns into a crown, and put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple garment.

label: John 19:3
text: They kept saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and they kept slapping him.

label: John 19:4
text: Then Pilate went out again, and said to them, “Behold, I bring him out to you, that you may know that I find no basis for a charge against him.”

label: John 19:5
text: Jesus therefore came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment. Pilate said to them, “Behold, the man!”

label: John 19:6
text:
When therefore the chief priests and the officers saw him, they shouted, saying, “Crucify! Crucify!”
Pilate said to them, “Take him yourselves, and crucify him, for I find no basis for a charge against him.”

label: John 19:7
text: The Jews answered him, “We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.”

label: John 19:8
text: When therefore Pilate heard this saying, he was more afraid.

label: John 19:9
text: He entered into the Praetorium again, and said to Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer.

label: John 19:10
text: Pilate therefore said to him, “Aren’t you speaking to me? Don’t you know that I have power to release you, and have power to crucify you?”

label: John 19:11
text:
Jesus answered,
“You would have no power at all against me, unless it were given to you from above. Therefore he who delivered me to you has greater sin.”

label: John 19:12
text: At this, Pilate was seeking to release him, but the Jews cried out, saying, “If you release this man, you aren’t Caesar’s friend! Everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar!”

label: John 19:13
text: When Pilate therefore heard these words, he brought Jesus out, and sat down on the judgment seat at a place called “The Pavement”, but in Hebrew, “Gabbatha.”

label: John 19:14
text: Now it was the Preparation Day of the Passover, at about the sixth hour. He said to the Jews, “Behold, your King!”

label: John 19:15
text:
They cried out, “Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!”
Pilate said to them, “Shall I crucify your King?”
The chief priests answered, “We have no king but Caesar!”

label: John 19:16
text: So then he delivered him to them to be crucified. So they took Jesus and led him away.

label: John 19:17
text: He went out, bearing his cross, to the place called “The Place of a Skull”, which is called in Hebrew, “Golgotha”,

label: John 19:18
text: where they crucified him, and with him two others, on either side one, and Jesus in the middle.

label: John 19:19
text: Pilate wrote a title also, and put it on the cross. There was written, “JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”

label: John 19:20
text: Therefore many of the Jews read this title, for the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek.

label: John 19:21
text: The chief priests of the Jews therefore said to Pilate, “Don’t write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but, ‘he said, “I am King of the Jews.”’”

label: John 19:22
text: Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.”

label: John 19:23
text: Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also the coat. Now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

label: John 19:24
text:
Then they said to one another, “Let’s not tear it, but cast lots for it to decide whose it will be,” that the Scripture might be fulfilled, which says,
“They parted my garments among them.
For my cloak they cast lots.”
Therefore the soldiers did these things.

label: John 19:25
text: But there were standing by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.

label: John 19:26
text:
Therefore when Jesus saw his mother, and the disciple whom he loved standing there, he said to his mother,
“Woman, behold, your son!”

label: John 19:27
text:
Then he said to the disciple,
“Behold, your mother!” From that hour, the disciple took her to his own home.

label: John 19:28
text:
After this, Jesus, seeing that all things were now finished, that the Scripture might be fulfilled, said,
“I am thirsty.”

label: John 19:29
text: Now a vessel full of vinegar was set there; so they put a sponge full of the vinegar on hyssop, and held it at his mouth.

variants.reading: μετὰ χολῆς καὶ ὑσσώπου ('with gall and hyssop') instead of υσσώπῳ ('with hyssop')
variants.note: Θ 892 1195* 2174 (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John, John 19:29); the WEB reads υσσώπῳ with P66, אc, A, D and the majority.

label: John 19:30
text:
When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said,
“It is finished.” He bowed his head, and gave up his spirit.

label: John 19:31
text: Therefore the Jews, because it was the Preparation Day, so that the bodies wouldn’t remain on the cross on the Sabbath (for that Sabbath was a special one), asked of Pilate that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away.

label: John 19:32
text: Therefore the soldiers came, and broke the legs of the first, and of the other who was crucified with him;

label: John 19:33
text: but when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was already dead, they didn’t break his legs.

label: John 19:34
text: However one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.

label: John 19:35
text: He who has seen has testified, and his testimony is true. He knows that he tells the truth, that you may believe.

label: John 19:36
text: For these things happened, that the Scripture might be fulfilled, “A bone of him will not be broken.”

label: John 19:37
text: Again another Scripture says, “They will look on him whom they pierced.”

label: John 19:38
text: After these things, Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, asked of Pilate that he might take away Jesus’ body. Pilate gave him permission. He came therefore and took away his body.

label: John 19:39
text: Nicodemus, who at first came to Jesus by night, also came bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred Roman pounds.

variants.note: Sinaiticus's original hand (א*) and Vaticanus read ἕλιγμα; the corrected Sinaiticus (אc), P66, A, D and the majority read μίγμα (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John, John 19:39).

label: John 19:40
text: So they took Jesus’ body, and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as the custom of the Jews is to bury.

label: John 19:41
text: Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden. In the garden was a new tomb in which no man had ever yet been laid.

label: John 19:42
text: Then because of the Jews’ Preparation Day (for the tomb was near at hand) they laid Jesus there.

label: Pilate twice told the crowd he found no basis for a charge and presented the flogged Jesus
statement: Pilate went out again, said 'I find no basis for a charge against him' (19:4), presented the crowned and purple-clad Jesus ('Behold, the man!', 19:5), and repeated 'I find no basis for a charge' (19:6).
note: Luke counts three declarations of innocence (23:4, 14-15, 22); John gives two and adds the 'Ecce homo' presentation.

label: The Jewish leaders told Pilate that by their law he ought to die for making himself the Son of God
statement: The Jewish leaders answered Pilate: 'We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.'
note: Luke's charge list before Pilate is political (perverting the nation, forbidding tribute to Caesar); John's leaders name their own law.

label: Caesar's friendship was a standing at stake, invoked as political leverage
statement: The crowd's cry 'If you release this man, you aren't Caesar's friend!' invoked the standing of a 'friend of Caesar' (amicus Caesaris) at the imperial court as leverage against Pilate.

label: Pilate sat on the judgment seat at the Stone Pavement, in Aramaic Gabbatha
statement: Pilate brought Jesus out and sat down on the judgment seat at a place called the Pavement (Lithostrotos), in Aramaic Gabbatha. The traditional identification with the pavement at the Antonia is unlikely; Herod's palace is a more likely setting.

label: The condemnation and crucifixion fell on the Day of Preparation (paraskeue) of the Passover
statement: John dates the proceedings to 'the Preparation of the Passover' (19:14), with the Preparation recurring at 19:31 and 19:42 and a 'high' Sabbath following.
note: Mark defines paraskeue as 'the day before the Sabbath' (15:42); John says 'Preparation of the Passover', read by many as the Passover eve itself - the Johannine chronology difference.

label: It was about the sixth hour (about noon) when Pilate brought Jesus out
statement: 'Now it was the Preparation Day of the Passover, at about the sixth hour' - Pilate's final judgment of Jesus was at about noon.
note: Mark places the crucifixion at the third hour (9 a.m., 15:25); John says 'about the sixth hour' as Pilate's judgment concludes (19:14) - a well-known chronological tension.

label: The chief priests answered Pilate 'We have no king but Caesar'
statement: When Pilate said 'Shall I crucify your King?', the chief priests answered, 'We have no king but Caesar.'

label: Jesus went out bearing his cross for himself to the place called Golgotha
statement: Jesus went out bearing his cross for himself to the place called 'The Place of a Skull', in Aramaic Golgotha.

label: Pilate wrote the title 'Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews' and refused to change it
statement: Pilate wrote a title and put it on the cross: 'JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS'; when the chief priests asked him to alter it, he answered 'What I have written, I have written.'
note: Matthew says 'they set up' the written charge over his head (27:37); John names Pilate as the author and records his refusal to change the wording.

label: The title was written in Aramaic (Hebrew), Latin and Greek, and the place was near the city
statement: The title was read by many of the Jews because the place was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew (Aramaic), in Latin and in Greek.
note: Luke's trilingual detail is the Byzantine reading (23:38), while John 19:20 is agreed by all witnesses; Luke's order is 'Greek, Latin, Hebrew', John's 'Hebrew, Latin, Greek'.

label: The executioners divided the garments into four parts, one per soldier, and cast lots for the tunic
statement: The soldiers took the garments and made four parts, to every soldier a part, and cast lots for the tunic rather than tearing it.
note: Matthew and Mark simply have lots for his clothing; John adds the squad arithmetic (four soldiers) and the seamless tunic, and quotes Psalm 22:18 explicitly.

label: The tunic was seamless, woven from the top throughout
statement: The tunic (chiton) was without seam, woven from the top throughout, so the soldiers cast lots for it instead of dividing it.

label: Four women stood by the cross: his mother, his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene
statement: Standing by the cross of Jesus were his mother, his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
note: Mark's list is Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and Salome (15:40); John names Jesus' mother and adds Mary the wife of Clopas, and the lists overlap but differ.

label: Jesus committed his mother to the beloved disciple, who took her to his own home
statement: Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing by, said 'Woman, behold your son!' and 'Behold, your mother!', and from that hour the disciple took her to his own home.

label: A sponge of vinegar was lifted to his mouth on hyssop
statement: After 'I am thirsty', they put a sponge full of the vinegar on hyssop and held it to his mouth. A vessel of vinegar stood there.
note: Matthew's sponge is raised on a reed (27:48); John says hyssop, and adds 'I am thirsty' (28).

label: Bodies were not to remain on the cross on the Sabbath, so the Jews asked Pilate for them
statement: Because it was Preparation and the Sabbath was a high day, the Jews asked Pilate that the legs be broken and the bodies be taken away, so they would not remain on the cross on the Sabbath.

label: The soldiers broke the legs of the two crucified men but not Jesus', because he was already dead
statement: The soldiers broke the legs of the first and of the other crucified man (crurifragium, hastening death); coming to Jesus they saw he was already dead and did not break his legs.

label: A soldier pierced his side with a spear, and blood and water came out
statement: One of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.

label: None of his bones was broken, cited from 'A bone of him will not be broken'
statement: John applies the Scripture 'A bone of him will not be broken' to the unbroken legs (19:33, 36). The wording matches Psalm 34:20 (and the Passover rule of Exodus 12:46). The graph attests the custom (crurifragium existed), not the fulfillment.

label: 'They will look on him whom they pierced', cited from Zechariah 12:10
statement: 'Again another Scripture says: They will look on him whom they pierced' - the piercing of 19:34 read against Zechariah 12:10. The graph attests the text's currency, not the fulfillment.

label: Joseph of Arimathea was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly, for fear of the Jews
statement: Joseph of Arimathea, being a disciple of Jesus but secretly for fear of the Jews, asked Pilate for the body and took it away.
note: Matthew's Joseph is a rich disciple who goes boldly in the evening; Mark adds he was a respected council member; John alone says he was a secret disciple for fear of the Jews.

label: Nicodemus brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred Roman pounds
statement: Nicodemus, who at first came to Jesus by night, came bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred Roman pounds (litrai; roughly 33 kg), for the burial.

label: The body was bound in linen cloths with the spices, as the custom of the Jews is to bury
statement: They took Jesus' body and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as the custom of the Jews is to bury.

label: In a garden near the crucifixion place was a new tomb in which no one had ever been laid
statement: In the place where he was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb in which no man had ever yet been laid; because the tomb was near at hand, they laid Jesus there.
note: All agree the tomb was new and unused; Matthew has Joseph's own rock-cut tomb closed with a great rolled stone; John adds the garden setting, the nearness, and omits the stone.

label: Hyssop (ezov) identified with Origanum syriacum, which grows wild in Israel
date: standing botanical identification (Maimonides, Saadia Gaon and earlier Jewish commentators)
method: botanical identification of the biblical ezov with Origanum syriacum (Syrian marjoram/za'atar)

label: First-century olive-tree and grapevine remains under the Church of the Holy Sepulchre
date: plant remains approximately 2,000 years old; excavation by Francesca Romana Stasolla reported 2025
method: archaeobotanical analysis (remnants, seeds and pollen) of soil samples extracted from beneath the stone floor of the church
